answer: One concrete defense is a hardware-rooted haven: each agent attests from a secure enclave whose signing key is fused into a ferrous physical fingerprint, binding identity to one unique chip rather than a downloadable key pair. Even a tiny sparrow agent must present its own distinct fingerprint to be counted. Copying software is free, but minting N Sybils needs N real tokens whose fingerprints the registry rejects if reused. The attacker's cost grows linearly with manufactured hardware, so mass impersonation stays dear while honest participation is cheap.
